text:
To: Heads of Department
From: Rosalind Achebe, Registrar
Subject: Examination invigilation

The summer examination period will run from 2 to 20 June, and invigilators are needed for each session. Heads of department are asked to nominate suitable staff by 15 April. [1] Nominees must complete a short briefing on the regulations, which will be held on 20 May and again on 22 May.

Invigilators will be [2] for their time at the standard hourly rate, and a lunch will be provided on days when sessions run past noon. [3] a candidate is suspected of malpractice, the invigilator should confirm the matter with the chief invigilator before taking any action. [4] the importance of fairness, I should be grateful for your cooperation in ensuring that all sessions are properly staffed.

choices: Experience of previous sessions is helpful but not essential, since new staff are paired with a colleague who has invigilated before.
Experience of previous sessions is essential but not helpful, since new staff are paired with a colleague who has not invigilated before.
Experience of previous sessions was helpful but not essential, since new staff were paired with a colleague who had invigilated before.
Experience of the regulations is helpful but not essential, since new staff are paired with a candidate who has invigilated before.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says nominees must attend a briefing, which fits a sentence about preparing inexperienced staff; only the first is coherent.
Staff are 'compensated for their time', meaning paid; the others do not fit.
'Where a candidate is suspected of malpractice' introduces the specific case in which the rule applies; 'whereas' contrasts, and 'wherein' and 'whereby' do not fit.
'Given the importance of fairness' uses 'given' as a preposition meaning considering.
